methods.name: findAll
methods.signature: public static function findAll(mixed $text, bool $acrossLines = false): array
methods.doc:
Finds CNIC numbers in free text, such as a chat message, a note or an
uploaded document, for example to mask them before logging.

Digits are read in groups (unbroken runs of digits). Groups may be
joined by any run of spaces or tabs, or by one mark (a hyphen or
Unicode dash, a dot, a slash or an underscore) with any spaces around
it: `35202 1234567 1`, `35202  1234567  1`, `35202 -1234567- 1`,
`35202_1234567_1`, `35202 - 1234567 - 1`, `352 0212 3456 71`,
`35202/1234567/1`. A line break never joins groups. A match is
consecutive whole groups that add up to exactly 13 digits, starting
with a province code (1-8); the search goes on after each match, so
`0300-1234567 35202-1234567-1` finds the CNIC. A group is never split,
so 13 digits inside a longer unbroken number (an IBAN, a card number)
never match. Digits may be ASCII, Urdu or Arabic-Indic, even mixed.

With `acrossLines: true`, a single line break (`\r\n`, `\r` or `\n`,
with any spaces around it) also joins groups, so a CNIC written over
several lines is found; a blank line never joins them. This can also
join numbers on consecutive lines, such as a list of amounts.

Accepting any grouping catches CNICs as people really type them, but
matches more that is not a CNIC: any 13 digits starting with 1-8 split
into groups this way (an account, order or tracking number, table
columns, a price list such as `8260 - 8048 - 2804 - 0`, a file name
such as `IMG_20261123_12345`, or two shorter numbers written together)
are found. validate() stays strict.

Offsets are in code points, so `mb_substr($text, $m->start, $m->end -
$m->start)` is `$m->raw`. Invalid UTF-8 bytes are first replaced as
`mb_scrub()` does.

```php
Cnic::findAll('CNIC: 35202-1234567-1, phone 0300-1234567');
// [CnicMatch(raw: '35202-1234567-1', digits: '3520212345671',
//   formatted: '35202-1234567-1', start: 6, end: 21)]
Cnic::findAll('id 352 0212 3456 71')[0]->digits; // '3520212345671'
Cnic::findAll("CNIC\n35202\n1234567\n1", acrossLines: true)[0]->formatted;
// '35202-1234567-1'
```

params.name: $text
params.doc: Any text

params.name: $acrossLines
params.doc: Also join digit groups across a single line break, as if it were a space; a blank line never joins them. Default false.

returns.doc: The matches in order, or `[]` (also for a value that is not a string). Never throws.

for the couriers' own statuses, and city names as customers and couriers
write them. There are no API clients: nothing is sent anywhere.

methods.name: mapStatus

Maps a courier's own status (its name, numeric ID or code, as the
courier documents it) to one status (Courier::PENDING, BOOKED,
PICKED_UP, IN_TRANSIT, OUT_FOR_DELIVERY, ATTEMPTED, UNDER_REVIEW,
DELIVERED, RETURNING, RETURNED or CANCELLED).

Matching ignores case and extra spaces. PostEx's "Attempt Made:
<reason>" history messages map to `attempted`. A numeric status may be
given as a string or as a non-negative whole number (`5` or `5.0`).

Only statuses the courier documents publicly are mapped: PostEx's API
guide and one Leopards status. TCS, M&P, Trax and BlueEx publish no
list, so they always return null, as does any status not in the list.
No API is called.

mapping and the status values may change in a minor release as other
couriers' lists are added.

in the city list, so orders can be matched against a courier's service
list.

Accepts the exact name in any case, short forms (`LHR`, `Khi`, `Pindi`,

cities in Urdu script.

Courier::normalizeCity('LHR');          // "Lahore"
Courier::normalizeCity('lyallpur');     // "Faisalabad"

entries.name: FbrInvoice
entries.doc:
FBR Digital Invoicing (DI): a builder that works out the sales tax on the
invoice JSON posted to PRAL's gateway, and an offline validator for the
rules that can be checked without FBR's reference APIs.

Built from PRAL's "Technical Specification for DI API", version 1.12 (last
updated 24 July 2025), and PRAL's "Error Message Guide (Sales)". Nothing
here talks to FBR: there is no HTTP client and no token handling. Values
that only FBR's reference APIs can confirm (provinces, HS codes, units,
rates, sale types, SRO numbers) are checked for presence, not against
FBR's lists, unless the app passes the lists it synced from those APIs
(`validate($invoice, ['reference' => [...]])`).

An invoice is the JSON object FBR expects, with its camelCase keys: an
associative array (as `json_decode($json, true)` gives) or a `stdClass`
(as `json_decode($json)` gives). `items` is a list. An empty PHP array is
read as an empty list, not as an object.

fields.doc: Version of PRAL's technical specification this class follows.

fields.doc: `invoiceType` values in the specification.

fields.doc: `buyerRegistrationType` values in the specification.

methods.name: expectedSalesTax
methods.doc:
The sales tax FBR expects on a line, in rupees, or null when the rate
is not a plain percentage or per-unit amount (spec §7, errors 0102,
0104, 0105):

- `N%` on Third Schedule goods: retail price × rate (0102);
- `N%` otherwise: value excluding sales tax × rate (0104);
- `Rs.N`: quantity × N (0105).

Rounded half up to the paisa (the specification allows 2 decimals and
gives no rounding rule).

params.name: $item
params.doc: A line of the invoice (array or object) with `rate` and `saleType`, `quantity`, `valueSalesExcludingST` or `fixedNotifiedValueOrRetailPrice`

returns.doc: Null for anything else. Never throws.

methods.name: build
methods.doc:
Builds an FBR digital invoice from your own fields, working out
`salesTaxApplicable` on each line where you leave it out (see
expectedSalesTax(); uses SalesTax::calculate()). Lines with a rate that
is neither `N%` nor `Rs.N` (`Exempt`, combined rates) get 0 unless you
give the tax.

`salesTaxWithheldAtSource`, `totalValues` and
`fixedNotifiedValueOrRetailPrice` default to 0, and `invoiceRefNo` and
`buyerNTNCNIC` to `''`, as in FBR's samples. Nothing else is filled in
or changed (other keys are kept); check the result with validate().

Also returns column totals in rupees (`quantity`,
`valueSalesExcludingST`, `salesTaxApplicable`,
`salesTaxWithheldAtSource`, `extraTax`, `furtherTax`, `fedPayable`,
`discount`), which are for your own records: the specification has no
invoice-level totals.

params.doc: The invoice fields (array or object) with an `items` list

returns.type: array{invoice: array<string, mixed>, totals: array<string, float>}|null
returns.doc: Null if `$input` is not an object with an `items` list of objects. Never throws.

methods.name: validate
methods.doc:
Checks an FBR digital invoice against the rules of PRAL's specification
(v1.12) and Error Message Guide that need no call to FBR, and returns
every problem with FBR's error code.

Checked: invoice type (0003, 0011), date format (0005, 0042, 0113) and,
with `today`, a future date (0043); seller and buyer NTN/CNIC (0401,
0402, 0009), self-invoicing (0058), names, provinces (0073, 0074),
addresses, buyer registration type (0012), the reference number of a
debit note (0026), the sandbox scenario, and on each line: HS code
(0044), rate (0020), unit, sale type (0013), required and valid amounts
(0021, 0023, 0024, 0098, 0300, 0302), SRO schedule and serial (0077,
0078), Third Schedule retail price (0090), extra tax on reduced-rate
goods (0091) and the sales tax arithmetic (0102, 0104, 0105, to within
one paisa).

Not checked, because they need FBR's data: registration status, whether
a province, HS code, unit, rate, sale type or SRO is in FBR's lists or
fits the others, and the original invoice of a debit note. Pass the
lists your app syncs from FBR's reference APIs as `reference` to check
provinces, sale types, units and HS code/unit pairs against them; FBR's
APIs are authoritative.

Options:
- `today` (string): `YYYY-MM-DD`, to reject invoices dated later (error
  0043); not checked when left out
- `reference` (array or object): lists synced from FBR's reference APIs
  (PRAL's `/pdi/v1/provinces`, `/pdi/v1/uom`, `/pdi/v2/HS_UOM`, sale
  types from `/pdi/v2/SaleTypeToRate` …). Each list given is checked,
  ignoring case and extra spaces; lists left out are not:
  - `provinces` (list of strings), e.g. `['PUNJAB', 'SINDH']`: the
    seller (0073) and buyer (0074) province
  - `saleTypes` (list of strings): each line's sale type (0013)
  - `uoms` (list of strings): each line's unit of measure (0099)
  - `hsUom` (map of HS code to a list of units), as FBR's HS_UOM API
    returns them, e.g. `['0101.2100' => ['Numbers, pieces, units']]`:
    each line's HS code must be listed (an error with no code) and its
    unit allowed for it (0099)

```php
FbrInvoice::validate($invoice, ['reference' => ['provinces' => ['PUNJAB', 'SINDH']]]);
```

methods.name: parseAmount
methods.doc:
Reads a rupee amount the way people type it in Pakistan, and returns it in
rupees, rounded half-up to the paisa. Returns `null` for anything that is
not exactly one non-negative amount; it never throws.

Accepted:
- digits, with or without grouping: `150000`, `150,000` (international) or
  `1,50,000` (Pakistani: groups of two, then three), and decimals
  (`1,234.50`, `.5`, `5.`); a grouping must be complete and consistent;
- Urdu (`۱۵۰۰۰۰`) and Arabic-Indic (`١٥٠٠٠٠`) digits, also mixed with
  0-9, and the Arabic decimal and thousands separators (`٫`, `٬`);
- one currency mark before or after the number: `Rs`, `Rs.`, `PKR` or `₨`
  (any case), and a trailing `/-` (`Rs. 5,000/-`);
- one shorthand unit after the number, with or without a space, in any
  case: `k`, `thousand(s)`, `hazar`, `ہزار` (× 1,000); `lakh(s)`, `lac(s)`,
  `لاکھ` (× 100,000); `crore(s)`, `cr`, `کروڑ` (× 10,000,000). Decimals
  work with units: `1.5 lakh` is 150,000 and `2.25cr` is 22,500,000;
- whitespace around and between the parts (spaces, tabs, line breaks and
  no-break spaces).

Rejected (`null`): empty input, negative or signed amounts (`-500`,
`+500`), ranges (`5-10k`), more than one number (`500 600`), two currency
marks or two units, leftover letters (`500 rupees`, `5kk`), grouping that
could be read two ways or is broken (`1,50`, `1.500,00`, `1,5000`),
amounts over Rs. 50 trillion (50 lakh crore), beyond which a number can no
longer hold every paisa exactly, and values that are not strings.

The arithmetic is done on the digits, so the result is exact: `1.005`
rounds to 1.01 and `1.5 lakh` is exactly 150000.

```php
Currency::parseAmount('Rs. 1,50,000/-'); // value 150000.0, raw 'Rs. 1,50,000/-'
Currency::parseAmount('2.25cr');         // value 22500000.0, raw '2.25cr'
Currency::parseAmount('5-10k');          // null
```

returns.doc: `value` and `raw`, or null if the input is not one amount

methods.doc:
Returns the administrative divisions of Pakistan, or of one province
(case-insensitive), sorted.

The list is the 30 divisions of the 2023 census: Punjab 9, Sindh 6,
Khyber Pakhtunkhwa 7 and Balochistan 8. Islamabad has no division, and
the census tables do not cover Azad Jammu and Kashmir or
Gilgit-Baltistan. Divisions created since the census (such as Gujrat in
Punjab) are not included.

unknown or invalid UTF-8 province gives an empty array. Never throws.

methods.doc:
Returns the division a district belonged to in the 2023 census, or
null if it is not known (case-insensitive).

Census-district caveat: only the 136 districts of the 2023 census have
a division here, under the name they had then (so `Quetta`, `Dera
Bugti` and `South Waziristan` work, and their successors do not).
Districts created after the census, and those of Azad Jammu and
Kashmir, Gilgit-Baltistan and Islamabad, return null.

Null, empty, unknown or invalid UTF-8 input returns null. Never throws.

methods.name: getTehsils
methods.doc:
Returns the tehsils (talukas, sub-divisions) of a district
(case-insensitive), sorted. Former district names such as `Quetta` and
`South Waziristan` work.

Census-district caveat: the data is the 591 tehsil-level units of the
2023 census, each recorded under the district it was in then. For a
district of the 2023 census this returns its census tehsils, even if
some have since moved to a new district (so `Rawalpindi` still lists
Murree). For a district created after the census it returns only the
tehsils an official source places in it, which can be an empty array.
Azad Jammu and Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan are not covered.

Null, empty, unknown or invalid UTF-8 input returns an empty array.
Never throws.

methods.name: getTehsilDistrict
methods.doc:
Returns the district a tehsil, taluka or sub-division was in at the
2023 census, or null (case-insensitive).

Census-district caveat: the result is the census district, which may
have been split since (a tehsil of `Quetta` is now in Quetta East or
Quetta West). A few names are shared by tehsils in different districts
(`Saddar`, `Sahiwal`, `Khanpur`); pass the province to tell them apart.
Returns null when the name is unknown or still matches more than one
district.

A null province (the default) searches every province; an empty or
unknown one matches nothing. Null, empty or invalid UTF-8 input
returns null. Never throws.

entries.name: IncomeTax
entries.doc:
Income tax on salary: the salaried rate table of the Income Tax Ordinance
2001 (First Schedule, Part I, Division I, clause (2), which applies when
salary is more than 75% of taxable income) for tax years 2020 to 2027,
each from FBR's consolidated Ordinance. A tax year runs from 1 July to
30 June and is named after the June it ends in. Amounts are computed
exactly in whole paisa.

methods.name: getSalarySlabs
methods.doc: Returns the salaried rate table for a tax year.

params.name: $taxYear
params.doc: e.g. `2026` (1 July 2025 to 30 June 2026); null for the current tax year

returns.doc: Null for a year that is not covered (or not an integer). Never throws.

methods.name: getSalaryYears
methods.doc: Which tax years getSalarySlabs() covers, oldest first.

methods.name: getTaxYear
methods.doc:
The tax year (July to June) that contains a date: the year, plus one
from July on.

params.name: $date
params.doc: `YYYY-MM-DD` or a DateTimeInterface (its own calendar date); null for today in the default time zone

returns.doc: Null for an invalid date. Never throws.

methods.name: calculateSalary
methods.doc:
Income tax on a salaried individual's taxable income for a tax year,
from the salaried rate table (see getSalarySlabs()). Tax is rounded
half up to the paisa, reading the amount as written.

With `includeSurcharge => true` it adds the section 4AB surcharge: a
percentage of the whole tax once taxable income exceeds Rs 10 million
(10% in tax year 2025, 9% for salaried individuals in 2026, none in
2027 or before 2025). Because it applies to the whole tax, one rupee
over Rs 10 million adds it in full. It is off by default in 2.x so
that existing results do not change, and will be on by default in 3.0.

Tax credits, exemptions, the separate pension rate, super tax and
withholding adjustments are not applied. This is an estimate, not tax
advice.

Options:
- `taxYear` (int): e.g. `2026`; takes precedence over `date`
- `date` (string `YYYY-MM-DD` or DateTimeInterface): a day in the tax year
- `includeSurcharge` (bool): add the section 4AB surcharge; default false
Without `taxYear` or `date`, today's tax year is used.

```php
IncomeTax::calculateSalary(12_000_000, ['taxYear' => 2026, 'includeSurcharge' => true]);
// tax 3381000, surcharge 304290, total 3685290, monthly 307107.5
IncomeTax::calculateSalary(1_800_000, ['taxYear' => 2026])->source;
// DataSource(id: 'income-tax-slabs', effectiveFrom: '2025-07-01', …)
```

params.name: $annualIncome

returns.doc: Null for an invalid amount or a tax year that is not covered. Never throws.

× 12`, and `monthly` is the tax to withhold each month.

params.name: $monthlySalary

returns.doc: Null for an invalid amount or a tax year that is not covered. Never throws.

entries.name: Input
entries.doc:
As-you-type formatters and checkers for form fields.

Each check*() method returns one of:
- `empty`: nothing entered yet
- `incomplete`: what has been typed so far can still become valid
- `valid`: complete and valid
- `invalid`: cannot become valid by typing more

None of these methods throw.

methods.doc:
Formats a mobile number as the user types: `0300-1234567`, or
`+92 300 1234567` when the user starts with the country code.

methods.name: checkPhone
methods.doc:
Checks a mobile number while the user is typing. The `03XX` prefix is
checked as soon as it is complete.

methods.name: formatIban
methods.doc: Formats an IBAN as the user types: uppercase, in groups of four, up to 24 characters.

methods.name: checkIban
methods.doc: Checks a Pakistani IBAN while the user is typing.

methods.doc:
Identifies and formats any Pakistani telephone number: mobile,
landline, UAN (`111`), toll-free (`0800`) and premium-rate (`0900`)
numbers. 0122 numbers are not recognised: no PTA document lists them
(see DATA.md). Returns null if the number is invalid.

methods.doc: Returns the kind of a Pakistani telephone number, or null if it is invalid.

methods.name: validateLandline
methods.signature: public static function validateLandline(mixed $phone, bool $services = false): bool
methods.doc:
Validates a Pakistani landline (fixed-line) number such as
`042-35761234`. With `services: true` it also accepts the
non-geographic service numbers a business may give as its landline:
UAN (`021-111-123-456`, `111-123-456`), toll-free (`0800-12345`) and
premium rate (`0900-12345`); analyze() tells them apart with its
`type` field.

```php
Numbers::validateLandline('042-35761234');                     // true
Numbers::validateLandline('021-111-123-456');                  // false
Numbers::validateLandline('021-111-123-456', services: true);  // true
```

params.doc: Number in local or international format; anything that is not a string gives false

params.name: $services
params.doc: Also accept UAN, toll-free and premium numbers (default false)

returns.doc: True for a valid landline number (or service number, with `$services`). Never throws.

Validates the format of a Pakistani passport number: two letters
followed by seven digits, e.g. `AB1234567`. Case, surrounding spaces
and spaces or dashes between the letters and digits are ignored.

DGIP does not publish the format, so this checks the common shape
only; other passport types may differ. See DATA.md in the repository.

entries.name: Quality
entries.doc:
Delivery-quality checks for cash on delivery and other courier use: how
complete an address is, and whether a phone number looks reachable.

fields.name: ADDRESS_WEIGHTS
fields.doc:
Points for each part of an address (an AddressPart: `city`,
`houseNumber`, `street`, `area`, `postalCode`, `landmark`). They add up
to 100. A postal code scores in full only when it is a known post
office code; an unknown one scores 5.

methods.name: scoreAddress
methods.doc:
Scores how complete a free-form Pakistani delivery address is, for
cash on delivery and other courier use.

Built on Address::parse(). It looks for a city, a house, plot or flat
number, a street, an area, a postal code and a landmark ("near",
"opp", "nazd", "qareeb", "سامنے" …), and adds up ADDRESS_WEIGHTS. A
postal code that is a known post office raises the score more than an
unknown one, and a post office in a different province from the city
lowers it (with a warning in `parsed->warnings`).

This is a heuristic: it says how much an address tells a rider, not
whether the address exists. Never throws.

methods.name: phoneRiskSignals
methods.doc:
Flags a phone number that a courier cannot reach by SMS or call, or
that looks made up (a PhoneRiskFlag). Pure heuristics on the number
itself: no list of real numbers, no personal data, no network call.

- `invalid`: not a Pakistani phone number.
- `landline`: a fixed-line number (no SMS, often unanswered).
- `not-mobile`: a UAN, toll-free or other service number.
- `repeated-digits`: the 7-digit subscriber part uses at most two
  different digits (`0300-0000000`, `0300-1111112`).
- `sequential-digits`: the subscriber part is a run such as `1234567`
  or `7654321`.
- `test-number`: a placeholder often typed into forms
  (`03XX-1234567`, `03XX-7654321`, `0312-3456789`).

A valid mobile number with nothing suspicious returns `[]`. Never
throws.

entries.name: RaastQr
entries.doc:
Raast QR codes: SBP person-to-person and EMVCo merchant QR payloads, per
SBP's "Standard for Interoperable QR Code for Person-to-Person and
Merchant Payments" v1.0. Encode the returned string with any QR library.

methods.name: createP2P
methods.doc:
Creates a Raast person-to-person QR payload (SBP P2P format `02`). It
matches the QR codes banking apps generate, so Easypaisa, JazzCash and
other apps can scan it.

Options:
- `iban` (string, required): the payee's Pakistani IBAN
- `amount` (int|float): fixed amount; makes the QR dynamic, which needs an expiry
- `expiresAt` (DateTimeInterface): expiry of a dynamic QR, as local time
- `expiresIn` (int|float|string): milliseconds, or `30m`, `12h`, `7d`, counted from `now`
- `bankName` (string, at most 25 characters), `particulars` (at most 30)
- `scheme` (string): defaults to `00`
- `now` (DateTimeInterface): defaults to the current time

throws.doc: if the IBAN is invalid, a field is too long, or an amount is given without an expiry

methods.name: tryCreateP2P
methods.doc: createP2P() without throwing: null where it would throw.

methods.name: createMerchant
methods.doc:
Creates an EMVCo merchant-presented QR payload per SBP's Pakistan QR
standard.

Options:
- `merchantAccount` (array, required): `['tag' => '28', 'fields' => ['00' => 'A000000736', '01' => $iban]]`,
  the template sub-fields your bank gives you; `tag` (26-51) defaults to `28`
- `merchantName` (string, required, at most 25 characters)
- `city` (string, required, at most 15 characters)
- `mcc` (4 digits, defaults to `0000`), `amount`, `dynamic` (bool)
- `billNumber`, `mobileNumber`, `reference`
- `dueDate` (DateTimeInterface) with `amountAfterDueDate`

throws.doc: if a field is missing, too long, or out of range

methods.doc: createMerchant() without throwing: null where it would throw.

methods.name: parse
methods.doc:
Parses a Raast QR payload (P2P format `02` or EMVCo merchant format

Pakistani QR code. Never throws.

methods.name: validate
methods.doc:
Checks whether a Raast QR code can be paid. Never throws. Errors: not
a Pakistani payment QR, checksum mismatch, a person-to-person QR with
no IBAN, an IBAN that fails its checksum, expired, or a fixed-amount QR
without an expiry. Warnings: an amount in a static QR (apps ignore it),
a QR that expires soon, or a merchant QR with no IBAN (`no-iban`):
merchant QRs may pay through the merchant's own scheme, so it is
valid, but the payee can't be checked from the QR. The result's `kind`
is `p2p`, `merchant`, or null when the text is not a Raast QR.

params.doc: The time to check the expiry against; defaults to now

Standard sales tax rates with the dates they applied, from 1 July 2019:
federal sales tax on goods (FBR), and sales tax on services in Punjab
(PRA), Sindh (SRB), Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KPRA), Balochistan (BRA) and
Islamabad Capital Territory (FBR). Reduced, higher and sector rates are
not included. Amounts are computed exactly in whole paisa.

methods.name: getRate
methods.doc:
Returns the standard sales tax rate for goods (federal, Sales Tax Act
1990) or for services in a province or Islamabad Capital Territory,
on a given date.

Query:
- `kind` (string, required): `goods` or `services` (SalesTax::GOODS, SalesTax::SERVICES)
- `province` (string): for services, Punjab, Sindh, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
  (`KP`, `KPK`), Balochistan or Islamabad Capital Territory (`ICT`,
  `Islamabad`). For goods it may be left out; Azad Jammu and Kashmir
  and Gilgit-Baltistan give null.
- `date` (string `YYYY-MM-DD` or DateTimeInterface, its own calendar
  date): defaults to today in the default time zone

Returns null for an unknown province or kind, an invalid date, or a
date before 1 July 2019. Never throws.

methods.name: calculate
methods.doc:
Adds sales tax to an amount, or splits it out when `inclusive` is set.
The tax is rounded half up to the paisa, reading the number as written
(`1.005` is Rs 1.01).

Options: a `rate`, or a `province` (and `kind`, default `services`,
and `date`) to use the standard rate from getRate():
- `rate` (int|float): percent, 0 to 100, at most 2 decimals; takes precedence over `province`
- `province` (string), `kind` (string), `date` (string|DateTimeInterface): as for getRate()
- `inclusive` (bool): true if `$amount` already includes the tax

When the rate was looked up, the result's `source` gives that rate's
period, law and official document; with your own `rate` it is null.

```php
SalesTax::calculate(1000, ['province' => 'Punjab', 'date' => '2026-11-18']);
// net 1000, tax 160, gross 1160, rate 16,
// source DataSource(id: 'sales-tax-rates', effectiveFrom: '2019-07-01', …)
```

returns.doc: Null if the amount, rate or province is invalid or no rate applies. Never throws.

methods.name: normalizeRomanUrdu
methods.doc:
Normalizes informal Roman Urdu spellings (`kia` to `kya`). Also applies
normalize() and converts Urdu and Arabic-Indic digits to English. A
capitalized word keeps its capital; all-caps words are left alone.

methods.name: slugify
methods.signature: public static function slugify(mixed $input, mixed $options = []): string
methods.doc:
Turns text into a URL slug: lower-case words joined by `-`.

Urdu letters are kept as they are (no transliteration: Urdu does not
write short vowels, so there is no single Roman spelling). Diacritics,
tatweel and zero-width characters are dropped, the Arabic look-alikes
ك ي ى become the Urdu ک ی ی, Urdu and Arabic-Indic digits become
`0-9`, and accented Latin-1 letters lose their accents (`é` to `e`,
`ß` to `ss`). Anything else separates words.

Options: `script` (`any`, the default, keeps Latin and Urdu letters;
`latin` keeps only `a-z`; `urdu` keeps only Urdu letters; any other
value is `any`). Digits are always kept.

params.name: $input
params.doc: The text; anything that is not a string gives `''`

params.name: $options
params.doc: `['script' => Text::SCRIPT_*]`

returns.doc: The slug, or `''` when nothing is left. Never throws.

methods.name: compareUrdu
methods.signature: public static function compareUrdu(mixed $a, mixed $b): int
methods.doc:
Compares two strings in Urdu alphabetical order, for usort().

Letters follow the Unicode CLDR collation for Urdu (`ur`, CLDR 49):
ا آ ب بھ پ پھ ت تھ ٹ ٹھ ث ج جھ چ چھ ح خ د دھ ڈ ڈھ ذ ر رھ ڑ ڑھ ز ژ س ش ص
ض ط ظ ع غ ف ق ک کھ گ گھ ل لھ م مھ ن نھ ں ںھ و وھ ہ ھ ۃ ء ی یھ ے. A letter
joined with ھ is a letter of its own (so بھ comes after every other ب
word). أ ؤ ۂ ئ ۓ sort as ا و ہ ی ے and come just after them when words
are otherwise equal, and diacritics only break ties, in CLDR's order.

Outside the Urdu letters: spaces and punctuation come first, then
digits digit by digit (Urdu, Arabic-Indic and ASCII digits are equal;
`10` comes before `2`), then Urdu letters, then other Arabic-script
characters (the look-alikes ك ي ى ه ة), then everything else by code
point, ignoring ASCII case. Strings that are still equal are ordered
by code point, so the result is 0 only for identical strings. The
order does not depend on intl or ICU.

params.name: $a
params.doc: A string; anything else is treated as `''`

params.name: $b
params.doc: A string; anything else is treated as `''`

returns.doc: -1, 0 or 1. Never throws.

methods.name: isRtl
methods.doc:
Whether text reads right to left: its first letter is from a
right-to-left script such as Urdu or Arabic. Digits, punctuation and
spaces are skipped, as in the Unicode bidirectional algorithm's
paragraph rule.

params.name: $text
params.doc: The text; anything that is not a string gives false

returns.doc: False when there is no letter. Never throws.

methods.name: wrapBidi
methods.signature: public static function wrapBidi(mixed $text, mixed $direction = self::BIDI_AUTO): string
methods.doc:
Wraps text in Unicode directional isolates, so a name or number in
one direction does not reorder the sentence around it (for example an
English order number inside an Urdu message).

Uses FIRST STRONG ISOLATE (U+2068) by default, RIGHT-TO-LEFT ISOLATE
(U+2067) for `rtl` and LEFT-TO-RIGHT ISOLATE (U+2066) for `ltr`,
closed with POP DIRECTIONAL ISOLATE (U+2069). Any other direction is
`auto`.

params.name: $text
params.doc: The text; anything that is not a string gives `''`

params.name: $direction
params.doc: Text::BIDI_AUTO, Text::BIDI_RTL or Text::BIDI_LTR

returns.doc: The wrapped text. Never throws.

methods.name: romanUrduKey
methods.doc:
A phonetic key for Roman Urdu, so that different spellings of the same
name or word match: `Mubeen` and `Mobeen`, `Muhammad`, `Mohammad` and
`Muhammed`, `Rehman` and `Rahman`, `Chaudhry`, `Chaudhary` and
`Chaudhery`. Compare keys, not the text.

Each word keeps its consonants, its first vowel sound and a vowel sound
at its end. Letters for one sound are merged (`kh`, `sh`, `ch`; `ph`
and `f`; `q`, `c` and `k`; `v` and `w`; `th` and `t`, `dh` and `d`),
doubled letters count once, `e` counts as `a`, `o` as `u`, and a final
`h` after a vowel is dropped. Accents are removed (compatibility
decomposition, as JavaScript's `normalize('NFKD')`, without the intl
extension) and anything other than Latin letters splits words. The key
is not meant to be shown: it is an opaque string.

Different names can share a key (`Hamid` and `Hamad`), so treat a match
as "probably the same", not proof. normalizeRomanUrdu() is a different
tool: it rewrites informal spellings into readable text.

```php
Text::romanUrduKey('Mubeen') === Text::romanUrduKey('Mobeen'); // true
Text::romanUrduKey('Muhammad Rehman'); // 'muhmd rahmn'
```

params.name: $text
params.doc: A name or other Roman Urdu text

returns.doc: The key, one part per word separated by spaces; `''` for text with no Latin letters or a value that is not a string. Never throws.

entries.name: Withholding
entries.doc:
Withholding income tax for persons on and not on FBR's Active Taxpayers
List (ATL), from FBR's Withholding Tax Rate Card for tax years 2025 to
2027: 231AB cash withdrawal, 236C sale and 236K purchase of immovable
property, 151 profit on debt, 150 dividends, 153 goods, services and
contracts, 154B social media income (from 2027) and 149 salary. Amounts
are computed exactly in whole paisa.

methods.name: getRates
methods.signature: public static function getRates(mixed $taxYear, mixed $section = null): array
methods.doc:
Every case FBR's Withholding Tax Rate Card lists for the covered
sections in a tax year (2025 to 2027), with its rates for persons on
and not on the Active Taxpayers List and its references.

```php
count(Withholding::getRates(2027, '153')); // 17
```

params.name: $taxYear
params.doc: The tax year (int), e.g. `2027`

params.name: $section
params.doc: Only this section, e.g. `'153'` (any case); null for every section

returns.doc: The cases in the rate card's order, or `[]` for a year that is not covered. Never throws.

methods.name: calculate
methods.signature:
public static function calculate(
    mixed $section,
    mixed $amount,
    mixed $atl,
    mixed $subType = null,
    mixed $taxYear = null,
    mixed $date = null,
    bool $lateFiler = false,
): ?WithholdingTax
methods.doc:
Income tax to withhold or collect under one section of the Income Tax
Ordinance 2001, for a person on or not on FBR's Active Taxpayers List
(ATL), from FBR's Withholding Tax Rate Card for tax years 2025 to 2027.

Covered: 231AB cash withdrawal, 236C sale and 236K purchase of
immovable property, 151 profit on debt, 150 dividends, 153 goods,
services and contracts, 154B social media income (from 2027) and 149
salary (the salaried rate table, as IncomeTax::calculateSalary()).

The rate for a person not on the list follows each case's own rule in
the Tenth Schedule: usually double, but a fixed rate (236C, and 151 in
2025), its own value bands (236K), or none (149; 231AB applies only to
them). The rate applies to the whole amount. Where FBR's card and the
Ordinance differ, the Ordinance is used and `statuteOverride` says so.

This is an estimate from the rate card, not tax advice: exemptions,
reduced-rate certificates, adjustable or final status and the many
cases not listed here are not applied.

```php
Withholding::calculate('236K', 60_000_000, atl: false, taxYear: 2027);
// WithholdingTax(rate: 14.5, tax: 8700000.0, nonAtlRule: 'slabs', …)
Withholding::calculate('231AB', 80_000, atl: false, taxYear: 2027)?->tax; // 640.0
Withholding::calculate('151', 10_000, atl: true, subType: 'bank-deposit', taxYear: 2027)?->tax; // 2000.0
```

params.name: $section
params.doc: Section of the Ordinance: `'231AB'`, `'236C'`, `'236K'`, `'151'`, `'150'`, `'153'`, `'154B'` or `'149'` (any case, spaces around it ignored)

params.name: $amount
params.doc: The payment (or, for 236C/236K, the value; for 149, the year's taxable salary) in rupees (int|float), 0 to one trillion

params.name: $atl
params.doc: True if the person is on FBR's Active Taxpayers List (a bool; anything else gives null)

params.name: $taxYear

params.name: $date
params.doc: A date in the tax year instead: `YYYY-MM-DD` or a DateTimeInterface

params.name: $lateFiler
params.doc: True for a person on the list who filed the return late. Changes the rate only where the year has a late-filer rate (236C and 236K in tax years 2025 and 2026). Default false.

returns.doc: The rate, tax and references, or null for an unknown section, case or tax year, an invalid amount, no tax year or date, or an `$atl` that is not a bool. Never throws.

entries.name: Zakat
entries.doc:
Zakat deduction at source in Pakistan: the nisab notified each year by the
Administrator-General Zakat (Ministry of Poverty Alleviation & Social
Safety) and conveyed to banks by SBP, Zakat years 1433 to 1447 AH
(2012-2026), and the 2.5% deducted from accounts at or above it.

This is the nisab for deduction from savings and similar bank accounts
under the Zakat and Ushr Ordinance 1980, not a religious ruling on
personal Zakat.

methods.name: getNisab
methods.signature: public static function getNisab(mixed $zakatYear = null, mixed $date = null): ?ZakatNisab
methods.doc:
The nisab for compulsory Zakat deduction at source for a Zakat year.

Give the year (`1447`, `'1447'`, or the notification's `'1446-47'`) or
a date; `$zakatYear` takes precedence. A Zakat year starts on 1
Ramazan; for a date on the first of the two days the notification
gives for it, the year is unknown and the result is null.

```php
Zakat::getNisab(zakatYear: 1447)?->nisab; // 503529
Zakat::getNisab(zakatYear: '1445-46')?->zakatYear; // 1446
Zakat::getNisab(date: '2025-06-01')?->nisab; // 179689
```

params.name: $zakatYear
params.doc: The Hijri year (int, or a string such as `'1447'`), or the label as the notification writes it (`'1446-47'`)

params.name: $date
params.doc: A day in the Zakat year: `YYYY-MM-DD` or a DateTimeInterface (its own calendar date)

returns.doc: The year's nisab, dates and sources, or null for a year that is not covered, an invalid or missing year or date, or an ambiguous date. Never throws.

methods.name: getYears
methods.doc: Every notified Zakat year, oldest first.

methods.name: deduction
methods.doc:
Zakat deducted at source from one account on the valuation date (1
Ramazan): 2.5% of the whole balance when it is at or above that year's
nisab, and nothing when it is below or the holder filed the exemption
declaration (Form CZ-50). Give the year or a date as for getNisab().

It applies to the accounts the Ordinance subjects to deduction at
source: savings, profit-and-loss sharing and similar accounts (asset
code 101). Current accounts and foreign currency accounts are not
deducted. It is not a religious ruling on how much Zakat a person owes.

```php
Zakat::deduction(600000, zakatYear: 1447);
// ZakatDeduction(zakatYear: 1447, nisab: 503529, balance: 600000.0,
//   deductible: true, reason: null, rate: 2.5, zakat: 15000.0, source: …)
Zakat::deduction(600000, zakatYear: 1447, exempt: true)?->zakat; // 0.0
```

params.name: $balance
params.doc: The account balance in rupees (int|float) at the start of the valuation date, 0 to one trillion

params.name: $zakatYear
params.doc: As for getNisab()

params.name: $date
params.doc: As for getNisab()

params.name: $exempt
params.doc: True if the holder filed the exemption declaration (Form CZ-50). Default false.

returns.doc: The deduction and its source, or null for an invalid balance, a year that is not covered, or an ambiguous date. Never throws.
